title: actions/upload-artifact is the one action in the release workflow not pinned to a commit
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** `release.yml` has four `uses:` lines (`.github/workflows/release.yml:53`, `:156`, `:168`, `:201`). The first three are pinned to a full commit SHA with the version in a trailing comment. `:201` is `actions/upload-artifact@v7`, a movable major tag.
- **[seen]** `ci.yml`, `release-plz.yml` and `release.yml` hold 17 `uses:` lines between them, and this is the only one not pinned to a SHA.
- **[seen]** The step runs in the `build` job (`release.yml:145`). Three steps follow it there: "Pin the checksum on main", which takes `secrets.RELEASE_PAT` (`release.yml:210-252`), "Create the release" (`release.yml:257-289`), and "A consumer can actually resolve it" (`release.yml:299`). The workflow grants `contents: write` (`release.yml:37-38`).
- **[seen]** Dependabot checks the `github-actions` ecosystem weekly (`.github/dependabot.yml:9-14`). #34 shows it already bumping a SHA pin in this repo, comment included (`release-plz/action` `a80d79e…` to `b8d6b54…`).
- **[seen]** No later step downloads the artifact. `gh release create` attaches `build/ModelpipeFFI.xcframework.zip` from disk (`release.yml:284-285`). A `workflow_dispatch` dry run skips every push-only step (`release.yml:211`, `:258`, `:300`), so the uploaded artifact is all the run leaves behind.

## What follows

- **[inferred]** Whatever commit `v7` points to when a build tag fires is the code that runs in the job that later holds the release PAT and publishes the release. An action can write to `$GITHUB_ENV` and `$GITHUB_PATH`, and later steps in the same job inherit both, so the unpinned code can reach beyond its own step.
- **[inferred]** While one step in that job floats, the pins on the other three `uses:` lines do not protect it.
- **[inferred]** Pinning adds no upkeep, because Dependabot already maintains the other pins.

## Fix

- Pin `release.yml:201` to a full commit SHA with the version as a comment, the same way `release.yml:53` does. As of 2026-09-25, `v7` and `v7.0.1` both point to `043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a`. Check again before committing.
- Keep the step, since it is the only output of a dry run.

## Refs

- #34
verification_notes: Verified at modelpipe-ffi origin/main 9fb41de. `git grep -n uses: origin/main -- .github/workflows` returns 17 lines: ci.yml 9, release-plz.yml 4, release.yml 4. Sixteen are SHA-pinned with a version comment. The only unpinned one is release.yml:201 `actions/upload-artifact@v7`, and it has been there since the first commit (88e2f80). The build job is at release.yml:145. RELEASE_PAT is used at release.yml:212-213 and 252, `gh release create` at 284-289, and the push-only `if:` lines are 211, 258 and 300. `permissions: contents: write` is at 37-38. dependabot.yml:9-14 covers the github-actions ecosystem. Commit 792f68f (#34, by dependabot[bot]) moved release-plz/action from a80d79e to b8d6b54 and kept the comment. No download-artifact appears in any workflow. The SHA comes from `gh api repos/actions/upload-artifact/git/ref/tags/v7` and `.../v7.0.1`, which both returned 043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a on 2026-09-25. That is live GitHub data, not repo content. Duplicate search (`pinned`, `upload-artifact`, `SHA`) over all issues found only #24, which is about the consumer-resolve download stall and does not cover pinning. PR #1 was the Dependabot bump from 4 to 7, closed and superseded. The GITHUB_ENV/GITHUB_PATH point describes GitHub Actions platform behaviour, not repo code. Out of scope for this repo: gglib has the same unpinned `actions/upload-artifact@v7` at ci.yml:74, 272 and 457, coverage.yml:130, and release.yml:452, 469, 804 and 815 (origin/main f07d7895). ggchat has it at ci.yml:157 and 370 (origin/main e190a4d). modelpipe has none.
problems: The 17 uses: lines check out, as do the single unpinned one at release.yml:201, build at :145, RELEASE_PAT at :210-252, create at :257-289, the push-only ifs at :211/:258/:300, contents: write at :37-38, dependabot.yml:9-14, and #34 (by Dependabot). The v7 and v7.0.1 tags both resolve to 043fb46d… today. (1) 'Two steps follow it there' is wrong: three do, the third being 'A consumer can actually resolve it' at release.yml:299. (2) 'release.yml uses four actions' should read four uses: lines; checkout appears twice. No duplicate found (#24 is unrelated).

title: A build tag with a prerelease suffix publishes a full release
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** The workflow fires on `build/v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+-*` as well as the plain form (`.github/workflows/release.yml:24-28`), so a build tag with a prerelease suffix runs the whole release.
- **[seen]** No step after the trigger reads the suffix. The version is the ref name minus `build/v` (`release.yml:263`). "Create the release" calls `gh release create "v${version}"` with `--target`, `--title`, `--notes-file` and `--generate-notes`, and without `--prerelease` (`release.yml:257-289`).
- **[seen]** modelpipe's matching step passes `--prerelease` when the tag contains a hyphen (mmogr/modelpipe `.github/workflows/release.yml:378-390` at `5b86e86`, added in mmogr/modelpipe#111). Its comment records two things: `gh release create` leaves `make_latest` out of the request unless `--latest` is passed, and the REST API then defaults it to true (`release.yml:364-371`).
- **[seen]** No prerelease build tag has been pushed yet. The remote holds `build/v0.1.0` through `build/v0.4.1`, and `v0.4.1` is the current Latest.

## What follows

- **[inferred]** Take a first candidate such as `build/v0.5.0-rc.1`. This workflow would publish `v0.5.0-rc.1` as a full release. By modelpipe's reading of the API, it would also take the Latest badge and be what `/releases/latest` returns, ahead of `v0.4.1`.
- **[inferred]** SwiftPM resolution is probably unaffected. A range with no prerelease bound should not admit a candidate, for example ggchat's `.upToNextMinor(from: "0.4.0")` (ggchat `Package.swift:25`). That SwiftPM rule is not verified here. The harm is to the release page and to anything that reads "latest".

## Fix

- In "Create the release", pass `--prerelease` when `version` contains a hyphen, as modelpipe does (mmogr/modelpipe `release.yml:381-390`).
- Optionally, say in the notes block (`release.yml:264-282`) that the release is a candidate.

## Refs

- mmogr/modelpipe#111
verification_notes: Verified at modelpipe-ffi origin/main 9fb41de. The triggers are at release.yml:24-28, with the prerelease pattern at line 28. `version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#build/v}"` is at 263. The notes block is 264-282. `gh release create` at 284-289 has no --prerelease, and there is no `prerelease` string anywhere in the repo's workflows. Compared against modelpipe origin/main 5b86e86. release.yml:72-74 has the same two tag patterns. The comment is at 364-377, and the "Create GitHub release" step at 378-390 builds the `prerelease=(--prerelease)` array for `*-*` (382-385). `git log -S--prerelease` points to 5765feb "chore(release): the version is 0.7.0-rc.1 (#111)". `git ls-remote --tags` shows build tags v0.1.0 through v0.4.1, all without a suffix, and `gh release list` shows v0.4.1 as Latest. ggchat origin/main e190a4d Package.swift:25 is `.upToNextMinor(from: "0.4.0")`. Not verified: GitHub's make_latest default and the gh CLI behaviour. For both I rely on modelpipe's comment, so the body attributes those claims to it. Also not verified: the SwiftPM rule that excludes prereleases from non-prerelease ranges, which the body says. Duplicate search (`prerelease`, `release`) found #21 (closed, a release-plz tagging problem) and #24 (open, a consumer-resolve stall). Neither covers this.
problems: All citations check out: the triggers at :24-28, the version at :263, the notes at :264-282, and gh release create at :284-289 without --prerelease. modelpipe's release.yml:364-371 comment and :378-390 step check out, as does its log (5765feb, #111). The remote tags are build/v0.1.0 to build/v0.4.1, with v0.4.1 the current Latest, and ggchat Package.swift:25 checks out. The unverified GitHub and SwiftPM behaviour is attributed or hedged. Labels are valid. No duplicate found.

title: The file-size gate counts comment and blank lines
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** `current_sizes` measures each non-test `src/**/*.rs` file with `wc -l` (`scripts/check_file_size.sh:40-46`). The gate fails any file over `BUDGET=300` (`:33`, `:70-86`) that the baseline does not list, and the committed `scripts/file-size-baseline.txt` is empty. Every line counts, whether blank, `//`, `///` or `//!`.
- **[seen]** The header says the gate should push toward "not 'write less' but 'decompose by responsibility'" (`:13-17`).
- **[seen]** It runs in CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:55`) and in `make enforce` (`Makefile:49`), which the release workflow also runs (`.github/workflows/release.yml:110`).
- **[seen]** Measured at `9fb41de` over the 11 files the gate scans: 1,570 lines in total, of which 705 are comment-only and 113 are blank, leaving 752 lines of code. The largest file by the gate's count is `src/pipe.rs`, at 259 lines: 100 of code and 138 of comment. `src/lib.rs` has 173 lines, 33 of them code. No scanned file contains a `/*` comment.
- **[seen]** modelpipe's copy counts the same way (mmogr/modelpipe `scripts/check_file_size.sh:40-46` at `5b86e86`).

## What follows

- **[inferred]** The gate charges documentation against the budget. `src/pipe.rs` has 41 lines of headroom by the gate's count and 200 by its code. Near the limit, the cheapest way to pass is to delete comments, which is the "write less" the header rules out.
- **[inferred]** Two files with the same code but different amounts of explanation get different results, so the number says little about how many responsibilities a file holds.

## Fix

- Count only lines that are neither blank nor comment-only, for example with `grep -cvE '^[[:space:]]*(//|$)'` per file inside `current_sizes`. No scanned file has a block comment, so a line-based rule is enough for now, and `--update` (`:48-55`) picks up the new count on its own.
- Say "code lines" in the messages (`:51`, `:66`, `:80`, `:83`, `:99`).
- Budget: design needed. By code lines, the largest file is `src/pair_error.rs` at 180, so 300 is a looser limit than it is today. Keep it or lower it, but use one number in both repos.
- Make the same change in modelpipe's copy so the two scripts follow one rule.
verification_notes: Verified at modelpipe-ffi origin/main 9fb41de. In scripts/check_file_size.sh: BUDGET=300 at :33, current_sizes (find src + wc -l, *_tests.rs excluded) at :40-46, --update at :48-55, the comparison loop at :70-86, the header rationale at :13-17, and the messages at :51, :66, :80, :83, :99. The gate is called from ci.yml:55, Makefile:49 (enforce) and release.yml:110 (`make enforce`). Line counts come from running `git show origin/main:<file>` on each non-test src .rs file, with blank lines matched by `^[[:space:]]*$` and comment-only lines by `^[[:space:]]*//`. Results for the 11 files (raw/code/comment/blank): pipe.rs 259/100/138/21, pair_error.rs 234/180/38/16, error.rs 229/129/89/11, lib.rs 173/33/134/6, pair.rs 149/90/48/11, status.rs 131/70/51/10, options.rs 126/46/69/11, identity_file.rs 97/27/61/9, watch.rs 82/44/28/10, runtime.rs 76/30/39/7, bin/uniffi-bindgen.rs 14/3/10/1. Totals: 1570/752/705/113. The `/*` count is 0 in every scanned file. modelpipe origin/main 5b86e86 scripts/check_file_size.sh is identical in logic (wc -l at :40-46, scanning modelpipe/src and modelpipe-cli/src). I could NOT verify that modelpipe is moving to counting code lines only: its tip still uses wc -l, and no modelpipe issue or PR matches file-size/code lines (searched all states). Cross-link the modelpipe issue once it is filed. Aside, left out of the body: the header at :19-24 says the baseline is NOT committed, but scripts/file-size-baseline.txt is tracked, empty (0 bytes), and was added in 88e2f80. gglib's scripts/check_rust_complexity.sh also counts with wc -l (:35-41 at f07d7895). Duplicate search (`file size`, `file-size`, `comment lines`, `budget`) found nothing.
problems: All citations check out: BUDGET at :33; current_sizes at :40-46; --update at :48-55; the loop at :70-86; the header at :13-17; the messages at :51, :66, :80, :83, :99; ci.yml:55; Makefile:49; release.yml:110. The baseline is committed and empty. I re-measured all 11 files, and the totals (1570/752/705/113) and the pipe.rs and pair_error.rs numbers match. modelpipe's copy counts the same way. When filed, cross-link modelpipe-18, whose corrected fix now carries modelpipe's gate change.

title: A reply in flight is cut when the phone locks or the app goes to the background
body:
This is a decision to revisit, not a defect: the code does what its comments and ADR 0002 say.

## What the code does

- **[seen]** `RootView` sends every `.background` scene phase to `model.scene(.background)`, with no platform check (`Sources/GGChatUI/RootView.swift:55-58`).
- **[seen]** That pass runs `hangUpEveryPipe()` (`Sources/GGChatUI/AppModel+Lifecycle.swift:31-45`), which first cancels and awaits `streamTask` (`:105-109`). The app has one `streamTask` (`Sources/GGChatUI/AppModel.swift:31`). The cancel is not gated on `isPipe`; only the loop after it is (`AppModel+Lifecycle.swift:110`).
- **[seen]** `testGoingToTheBackgroundKeepsThePartialReplyInsteadOfLosingIt` pins the cut for a server added by address (`Tests/GGChatUITests/AppModelLifecycleTests.swift:141-164`, provider at `:146`, assertion at `:159`).
- **[seen]** `BackgroundAssertion` is taken before the hang-up and ended when it returns (`AppModel+Lifecycle.swift:37-42`). It buys time to put the reply down and hang up, not to let the reply finish (`Sources/GGChatUI/BackgroundAssertion.swift:5-24`, `:30-49`).
- **[seen]** The rationale is that a held pipe's status is only as fresh as the last thing that arrived over a socket the system may have reclaimed (`AppModel+Lifecycle.swift:83-91`). ADR 0002 accepts partial-plus-Continue as the outcome (`docs/adr/0002-an-in-flight-request-is-kept-not-re-sent.md:121-133`), and Continue re-sends the conversation (`:36-38`).

## What follows

- **[inferred]** Locking the phone mid-reply leaves a partial; getting the rest costs a Continue and a second request.
- **[inferred]** The rationale is about idle pipes. A pipe carrying a reply has bytes arriving, and while an assertion holds the process is not suspended, so the staleness argument does not reach it.
- **[inferred]** It does not reach servers added by address at all. They have no pipe and no pill, and their replies are cut the same way.

## Fix

- Design needed: hang up idle pipes at once, but keep the reply and the one pipe carrying it for as long as a background grace lasts, cutting only when the grace expires.
- Decide whether macOS cuts at all; `BackgroundAssertion.swift:26-28` says a Mac app is not suspended.
- Amend ADR 0002's reading, since a reply that finishes in the background is no longer a mid-reply close.

## Refs

- #83, the other way the client cuts a live reply short; its one configured `URLSession` is where a reply's time limits would be set.
verification_notes: Read at ggchat origin/main e190a4d. RootView.swift:55-65 onChange(scenePhase): .active -> scene(.foreground) at :57, .background -> scene(.background) at :58, no #if. AppModel+Lifecycle.swift:31-45 background pass (isAway, cancels resume, BackgroundAssertion at :37, hangUpEveryPipe at :41, assertion.end at :42); hangUpEveryPipe :104-113, reads streamingProviderID at :105, cancels+awaits streamTask at :106-109 with no isPipe check; loop gated on config.isPipe at :110. Rationale comment :83-91 (TN2277, stale status, 'Direct' over nothing), partial-write paragraph :93-96. AppModel.swift:31 single `var streamTask`. BackgroundAssertion.swift doc :5-28 (macOS: 'a Mac app is not suspended' :26-28), struct :29-50. BackgroundAssertion is also used at AppModel+Pipe.swift:132 for a dial landing while away; neither use covers a reply. AppModelLifecycleTests.swift:141-164 uses .openAICompatible provider (:146) and asserts !isStreaming (:159). ADR 0002 :121-133 (suspension mid-reply is counted; partial + Continue), :36-38 Continue re-sends the conversation. No UIBackgroundModes/BGTaskScheduler anywhere in the repo (git grep, 0 hits). Duplicate search (background reply, phone locks, background cancel, BackgroundAssertion, hang up background): only closed #69 (a race between hang-up and resume, fixed) - not this. #83 (URLSession.shared 60s timeout) and #85 (removeProvider leaves a reply streaming) are related but distinct. Inferred, not verified on device: that a screen lock delivers .background, and what SwiftUI reports as .background on macOS.
problems: All citations check out: RootView.swift:55-58; Lifecycle :31-45, :105-110, :37-42 and :83-91; AppModel.swift:31; the test at :141-164 (with :146 and :159); BackgroundAssertion.swift:5-24, 26-28 and 30-49; ADR 0002 :36-38 and :121-133. The only problem is the component label. In ggchat, 'app' means the Xcode app target, but every file cited is in GGChatUI, so it should be 'ui'. No duplicate found (#69 is closed and different; #83 is related).

title: The app cannot use tools: requests carry role and content only
body:
## What the code does

At `e190a4d`:

- **[seen]** A request message is a role and a string: `WireMessage { role: String; content: String }` (`Sources/GGChatCore/Wire.swift:150-153`), built from each `Message` at `:168`. `ChatCompletionRequest` encodes `model`, `messages`, `stream`, `stream_options` and `max_tokens`, and nothing else (`:143-148`, keys at `:160-164`).
- **[seen]** `Role` has `system`, `user` and `assistant` (`Sources/GGChatCore/Models.swift:3-7`). There is no `tool`.
- **[seen]** A streamed `Delta` decodes `content` and `reasoning_content` only (`Wire.swift:132-139`). `ChatEvent` is `delta`, `reasoning`, `finished` or `error` (`Sources/GGChatCore/ChatEvent.swift:2-7`), and the model ignores the finish reason (`Sources/GGChatUI/AppModel+Streaming.swift:112`).
- **[seen]** `git grep` finds no `tools`, `tool_calls`, `tool_call_id` or `tool_choice` in `Sources` or `App`.
- **[seen]** The app's own fixture of gglib's status shows gglib translating a model's dialect to OpenAI `tool_calls` and counting tool repairs (`Tests/GGChatCoreTests/Fixtures/gglib-proxy-status.json:1`).

## What follows

- **[inferred]** No model can be offered a function from this app, and a tool call could not be read, shown, answered or stored if one arrived. The server's tool support is out of reach from the phone.
- **[inferred]** The change reaches every layer: the wire, `Role` and `Message`, the stream parser (tool-call deltas arrive in fragments), `MessageRecord` (`Sources/GGChatUI/Persistence/Records.swift:56-68`) and the transcript.

## Fix

- Design needed: which tools exist, where they run, and whether a person approves each call. gglib answers `/mcp` through the tunnel only when the desktop's owner turned it on with `gglib remote enable --allow-mcp`, and otherwise refuses with `mcp_not_allowed_over_tunnel` (gglib `crates/gglib-proxy/src/remote/mcp_guard.rs:16-47` at `f07d7895`; here `Sources/GGChatCore/ProviderError.swift:125`), so the desktop's MCP servers are one source, off by default.
- `tools` on the request, and `tool_calls` on the delta, accumulated per index.
- A `tool` role with `tool_call_id`, and calls and results stored and drawn.
- A request loop that continues while `finish_reason` is `tool_calls`.
verification_notes: Read at ggchat origin/main e190a4d. Wire.swift:143-171 ChatCompletionRequest (fields :144-148, WireMessage :150-153, CodingKeys :160-164, init mapping :168); Delta :132-139; Models.swift:3-7 Role; ChatEvent.swift:2-7; AppModel+Streaming.swift:112 `case .finished: finished = true`; OpenAICompatibleProvider+Streaming.swift:67 keeps finish_reason but only for the .finished event. git grep counts (0) for tool_calls, tool_call_id, tool_choice across Sources/App/Tests excluding Fixtures, and 0 for -w 'tools' in Sources/App. The only repo hits for tool terms are inside the gglib status fixtures (gglib-proxy-status.json:1 and .sse:1,3,5), which contain tool_repairs_attempted and the launch decision 'qwen-xml -> OpenAI tool_calls'. Records.swift:56-68 MessageRecord. ProviderError.swift:125 mcpNotAllowedOverTunnel. Duplicate search (tools, tool calls, tool_calls, function calling): no match; #87 (client basics) does not mention tools. Not verified: whether gglib's MCP refusal covers every MCP route over the tunnel (inferred only from the code's name).
problems: The Wire, Models, ChatEvent, AppModel+Streaming, Records and fixture citations and the greps check out. (1) The MCP sentence misleads. gglib refuses /mcp over the tunnel only unless the owner ran `gglib remote enable --allow-mcp` (gglib crates/gglib-proxy/src/remote/mcp_guard.rs:16-47), so the desktop's MCP servers are a possible source, off by default. The drafter's notes flagged this as unverified. (2) The labels miss 'ui': MessageRecord, the transcript and the streaming loop live in GGChatUI. They also miss 'decision', since which tools exist, where they run and who approves each call needs an ADR. (3) ggchat PR #135 will move ProviderError.swift lines, so the body now pins e190a4d. No duplicate found.

title: The app cannot send images
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** A request message's `content` is a `String` (`Sources/GGChatCore/Wire.swift:150-153`), built from `Message.content` at `:168`. `Message.content` is a `String` (`Sources/GGChatCore/Models.swift:16`), and so is the stored `MessageRecord.content` (`Sources/GGChatUI/Persistence/Records.swift:59`).
- **[seen]** The one way a person adds a message is `send(_ text: String)` (`Sources/GGChatUI/AppModel+Streaming.swift:41-48`).
- **[seen]** `git grep` at e190a4d finds no `image_url` anywhere in the repo, and no `PhotosUI`, `fileImporter`, `dropDestination`, `UIImage` or `NSImage` in `Sources` or `App`.
- **[seen]** `ModelInfo` decodes `id`, `owned_by`, `description` and `context_window` (`Wire.swift:3-22`). Nothing in it says whether a model accepts images.
- **[seen]** gglib tags a model `vision` (gglib `crates/gglib-core/src/domain/capability_tags.rs:59-60` at `f07d7895`), but `mmproj` appears nowhere in its tree: no code there asks llama-server to load the projector a vision model reads images with.

## What follows

- **[inferred]** A photo, a screenshot or a scanned page cannot be put in front of a vision model from the phone, the device with the camera.
- **[inferred]** Through gglib, the server this app is built around, an image also needs a gglib change before anything reads it; a server added by address may take one today.
- **[inferred]** The change reaches the wire, the model types, storage and the composer at once, because a plain string is the type at each.

## Fix

- On the wire, `content` becomes either a string or an array of parts (`text`, and `image_url` with a `data:` URL). Text-only messages keep the string.
- `Message` gains attachments, stored outside the row, with a SwiftData migration.
- A picker and a drop target in the composer, with a size cap and a downscale before encoding.
- Design needed: how the app learns that a model takes images. `/v1/models` as decoded here does not say, so either gglib publishes it (and loads a projector) or a refusal is shown as one.
verification_notes: Read at ggchat origin/main e190a4d. Wire.swift:150-153 WireMessage content: String, :168 mapping; Models.swift:16 `public var content: String`; Records.swift:59 MessageRecord content String; AppModel+Streaming.swift:41-48 send(_ text: String). git grep: image_url 0 hits in the whole tree; PhotosUI, fileImporter, dropDestination, onDrop, NSItemProvider, UIImage, NSImage, 'data:image' all 0 in Sources and App (the 33 case-insensitive 'image' hits are all systemImage/Image(systemName:) and VisionKit for ticket scanning). Wire.swift:3-22 ModelInfo fields. Duplicate search (image, images, vision, attachment, multimodal): no match. Not verified: whether gglib's /v1/models exposes any vision capability field (not read).
problems: The Wire, Models, Records and AppModel+Streaming citations and the greps check out. (1) The draft does not check the server side. gglib, the app's main server, tags models `vision` (capability_tags.rs:59-60), but `mmproj` appears nowhere in gglib's tree at f07d7895. So through gglib an image has no projector to read it, and the feature needs a gglib change too; servers added by address may work today. (2) The labels miss 'ui': the composer and MessageRecord storage are in GGChatUI. No duplicate found.

title: gglib's error codes are hand-typed here, while modelpipe's are vendored and digest-pinned
body:
## What the code does

Line numbers here are at `e190a4d`.

- **[seen]** `ProviderError.Code` is the app's closed vocabulary: seven modelpipe codes (`Sources/GGChatCore/ProviderError.swift:98-113`) and eighteen gglib codes (`:115-134`).
- **[seen]** The modelpipe half is checked against `Tests/GGChatCoreTests/Fixtures/modelpipe-error-codes-v0.json`, vendored from modelpipe's `docs/error-codes-v0.json` and pinned by a SHA-256 digest (`Tests/GGChatCoreTests/ErrorTests.swift:42-49`), then compared with the enum (`:68-70`).
- **[seen]** The gglib half is a hand-typed set in the same test (`ErrorTests.swift:61-67`). It is checked only for being disjoint from the modelpipe half and for covering the rest of `allCases` (`:71-74`). Its source is named in a comment, `gglib-proxy`'s `ErrorResponse` constructors (`ProviderError.swift:115-116`).
- **[seen]** gglib at f07d7895 has no code-list file. Its codes are string literals, most passed to `ErrorResponse::with_code` (`crates/gglib-proxy/src/models.rs:422`) from four non-test files. Each of the eighteen appears there today.
- **[seen]** A code the vocabulary does not know reads as `.unknown` (`ProviderError.swift:64-70`) and gets no hint of its own (`:77-80`).

## What follows

- **[inferred]** A code gglib adds or renames fails no test here; gglib's own tests change with it. It reaches the person without its own hint, and nothing prompts anyone to add it here.
- **[inferred]** The two halves of one vocabulary carry different guarantees: one is checked against its publisher byte for byte, the other against memory.

## What the code does

- **[seen]** `save(conversation:)` assigns `content`, `reasoning`, `isPartial`, `failureData` and `order` on every message row already stored (`Sources/GGChatUI/Persistence/SwiftDataStore.swift:138-146`), after encoding each message's failure to JSON (`:140`), whether or not anything changed. - **[seen]** It runs through `AppModel.update` and `persist` (`Sources/GGChatUI/AppModel.swift:170-181`). ## What follows

- **[inferred]** Each turn saves twice, once as it is sent and once as it ends, and each save walks and assigns every row of the conversation, so a turn costs more as the conversation grows, though only one or two rows changed.

- Assign a field only when it differs from the stored value, and encode `failureData` only for a message whose failure changed.

title: The connect side holds its in-flight guard across the whole copy_bidirectional, so a local client that keeps its socket open holds shutdown
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** `carry` takes the in-flight guard once the client has sent a byte (`modelpipe/src/dialer.rs:193-194`) and holds it until `copy_bidirectional` returns (`dialer.rs:224-226`). Only the peek watches for teardown (`dialer.rs:178-192`).
- **[seen]** The comment above the copy says it "finishes when both halves have seen EOF, which for one exchange per stream is exactly when the response is complete" (`dialer.rs:221-223`).
- **[seen]** The serve side ends its half with `finish` (`modelpipe/src/listener.rs:257-261`), and every proxied response carries `Connection: close` (`modelpipe/src/exchange.rs:279-281`).
- **[seen]** `shutdown` waits on `wait_until_drained` with no deadline (`dialer.rs:271-273`); `shutdown_timeout` bounds it (`dialer.rs:291-295`). `ConnectHandle::shutdown` promises to "let the in-flight requests finish" and "does not time out" (`modelpipe/src/connect_handle.rs:209-217`).
- **[seen]** The CLI's `connect` calls `shutdown()` (`modelpipe-cli/src/main.rs:73`), and only a second interrupt stops that wait (`modelpipe-cli/src/park.rs:201-207`).
- **[seen]** The connect-side drain test covers a socket that never sends a byte (`modelpipe/tests/integration_pipe.rs:770-790`), not one that has had its response.

## What follows

- **[inferred]** `finish` ends only the remote-to-local half. The other half ends on the local client's EOF, so the guard measures "the client's socket is open", not "the response is written".
- **[inferred]** A client that honours `Connection: close` closes at once. One that does not (a pool that has not noticed the FIN, a hand-rolled client, a stopped process) holds `shutdown` until it closes, which may be never. In the CLI, the first Ctrl-C then waits on it.
- **[inferred]** Under `shutdown_timeout`, which modelpipe-ffi (`src/pipe.rs:213`) and gglib (`crates/gglib-app-services/src/remote/connect.rs:154-156`) both call, the whole grace is spent and `false` returned for an exchange that had finished; gglib then warns that requests were cut.

## Fix

- Design needed: what "response fully written" means in a copy that does not parse HTTP. The response half ending is the obvious signal, but a backend can answer before the request body ends (an early 4xx).
- One shape: two directional copies in place of `copy_bidirectional`, the guard dropped when the response half finishes, and the request half given a short deadline, as `refuse_locally` has `REFUSAL_DRAIN` (`dialer.rs:246-268`).
- Until then `shutdown_timeout` bounds it; the `ConnectHandle::shutdown` doc should say the drain waits for local clients to close.
- A test beside `integration_pipe.rs:770`: a client reads its response, keeps the socket open, and `shutdown` must still return.

title: The private-file checks look at mode bits only, so a file owned by another user passes
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** `check_private` reads `fs::metadata(path)` and accepts the file when `mode & 0o077 == 0` (`modelpipe/src/private_file.rs:172-186`). Nothing compares the owner's uid with this process's.
- **[seen]** The CLI has two more checks of the same shape, for the devices file (`modelpipe-cli/src/devices.rs:101-116`) and the state folder (`modelpipe-cli/src/state.rs:250-265`). Neither looks at the owner.
- **[seen]** Each runs after the path has been read or made: the identity file is read at `modelpipe/src/identity.rs:69` and checked at `:92`; the devices file is read then checked at `devices.rs:22-24`; the folder is made then checked at `state.rs:139-140`.
- **[seen]** `SECURITY.md` calls these checks "a floor, not a guarantee" (`SECURITY.md:88-93`).

## What follows

- **[inferred]** For a process that is not root the gap is narrow: a 0600 file owned by another user fails the read with EACCES before any check runs, and a 0700 folder owned by another user fails when the lock file inside it is opened (`state.rs:141-145`).
- **[inferred]** The exposure is a process running as root. It reads another user's 0600 key, devices file or folder, accepts it, and serves with secrets that user can read and rewrite.
- **[inferred]** On macOS an ACL entry is not reflected in the mode bits, so a 0600 file whose ACL grants another user read passes too. Linux shows a POSIX ACL's mask in the group bits, which the check does see. Not tested.

## Fix

- Refuse a file or folder whose owner is not the effective uid, in all three checks, with a message naming the owner.
- The workspace denies `unsafe` (`Cargo.toml:43`), so the euid needs a safe wrapper. rustix's `process` feature is one; the CLI already depends on rustix (`modelpipe-cli/Cargo.toml:66`), but for the library it is new compilation, which its manifest argues about dependency by dependency.
- ACLs: design needed, or say in `SECURITY.md` that the checks read mode bits and ownership only.

## Refs

#98, #103

title: A chunk extension is forwarded verbatim with any control character in it
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** `forward_chunked` reads a size line up to CRLF (`modelpipe/src/body.rs:73-87`), checks only the text before the first `;` (`body.rs:151-171`), and writes the whole line on unchanged (`body.rs:173-174`). Extensions "are not ours to interpret" (`body.rs:152`), and a test pins the pass-through (`modelpipe/src/body_tests.rs:182-189`).
- **[seen]** The same function carries the request body to the backend (`modelpipe/src/request_body.rs:146`) and the response body to the client (`modelpipe/src/exchange.rs:289`).
- **[seen]** Trailer lines are dropped for a bare CR or LF (`body.rs:264-267`) and checked for no other control byte.

## What follows

- **[inferred]** NUL, the other C0 controls and DEL in an extension reach the next hop in either direction. RFC 9112 §7.1.1 admits none of them: an extension name is a token, and a value a token or quoted-string, whose only allowed control is HTAB.
- **[inferred]** Refusing a bare CR or LF in the size line is planned separately, and it is the part that splits lines. No parser is known to split on the rest, so this is hardening rather than a known smuggling path: it removes bytes a lenient or C-string parser downstream might read differently from this edge.
- **[inferred]** It is the extension-side twin of #100: the line goes on verbatim, so whatever this edge tolerates, the next hop receives.

## Fix

- Refuse a size line whose extension holds a byte in 0x00-0x08, 0x0A-0x1F or 0x7F, through the same error as a bad size. HTAB stays.
- Decide whether trailer lines get the same rule.
- Cases beside `body_tests.rs:182-203`; the fuzz target #72 asks for would cover this line too.

## Refs

#100, #72

title: eprintln! and println! panic the CLI when a write to stderr or stdout fails
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** The CLI prints status lines with `eprintln!` at 17 call sites under `modelpipe-cli/src/`: `diagnostics.rs:106`, `main.rs:60`, `pairing.rs:34, 43, 58, 106, 187, 191, 199, 221`, `park.rs:205`, `serve_cmd.rs:66, 93, 135, 146, 182` and `serve_out.rs:163`. `park.rs`'s three other mentions are doc comments.
- **[seen]** `report` writes the live status lines with `writeln!` and drops the error, "which is more than the `eprintln!` this replaced offered, since that panicked" (`park.rs:112-121`).
- **[seen]** Two of the 17 run after startup: `pairing.rs:106`, in the invite watcher spawned at `serve_cmd.rs:173-178`, and `park.rs:205`, on a second interrupt during shutdown. `main` is `#[tokio::main]` (`main.rs:26`).
- **[seen]** stdout gets the ticket (`serve_cmd.rs:110`), then the token or pairing line (`serve_out.rs:162`, `serve_cmd.rs:134`), then the QR code unless `--no-qr` (`serve_cmd.rs:154-155`); the README offers `modelpipe serve … | head -1` (`README.md:263-264`).

## What follows

- **[inferred]** Rust ignores SIGPIPE, so writing to a pipe with no reader returns EPIPE; a hung-up terminal gives EIO and a full disk ENOSPC. `eprintln!` panics on any of them. A closed fd 2 does not: std treats EBADF on stderr as success.
- **[inferred]** At startup that is `serve` exiting with a panic, before it listens (`serve_cmd.rs:66`, `:93`) or just after (`serve_cmd.rs:135`, `:146`, `serve_out.rs:163`), under a supervisor whose log pipe has gone or with stderr on a full disk.
- **[inferred]** Later, the invite watcher's task panics after `settle` has done its work, losing only the line; a panic at `park.rs:205` ends the process with status 101 instead of a clean exit.
- **[inferred]** `println!` behaves the same. Under `| head -1`, `head` can exit after the ticket, and a later stdout line such as the QR code then panics the listener. Whether it does is a race on when `head` exits.

## Fix

- One helper for status lines that writes to stderr and drops the error, as `report` does, in place of the 17 calls.
- stdout: a failed ticket line should end `serve` with an error rather than a panic; decide whether later stdout lines drop theirs.
- Deny `clippy::print_stderr` and `clippy::print_stdout` in the CLI crate so the macros do not come back.

title: A page on another site can drive the daemon's and the proxy's POST routes that do not require a JSON Content-Type
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** A loopback daemon asks for no credential: `resolve_daemon_api_key` returns `None` for a loopback bind (`crates/gglib-axum/src/daemon/mod.rs:246-249`), and `bearer_policy` turns that into `BearerPolicy::fixed(None)` (`crates/gglib-axum/src/access.rs:113-119`).
- **[seen]** `host_guard` reads only `Host` (`access.rs:127-140`). A page posting to `127.0.0.1:9887` sends a loopback `Host`.
- **[seen]** `/api/*` sits behind an origin allowlist (`daemon/mod.rs:36-43,75`, `routes.rs:31-38,375-378`). CORS hides the response from a page; it refuses no request.
- **[seen]** axum 0.8.9 (`Cargo.lock:314-315`) refuses `Json` without a JSON `Content-Type` (`axum-0.8.9/src/json.rs:106-109`). These daemon POST handlers take no `Json` (under `crates/gglib-axum/src/handlers/`): remote disable, invite, disconnect (`remote/mod.rs:42`, `remote/devices.rs:98`, `remote/connect.rs:27`); shutdown (`daemon.rs:19`); proxy stop (`proxy/mod.rs:197`); install, setup-python, disable-fast-downloads, check-updates, uninstall and update llama.cpp (`config/setup.rs:38,78,85,148,160,189`); MCP start, stop, test, resolve (`mcp.rs:48,56,69,99`); add tag, apply upgrade (`model/models.rs:139,209`); verify (`model/verification.rs:48`); download cancel, shard-group cancel, clear failed (`model/downloads.rs:93,128,137`); tune apply (`benchmark/tune.rs:110`).
- **[seen]** The proxy is keyless on loopback until a key is stored (`crates/gglib-runtime/src/proxy/api_key.rs:48-49`). In `crates/gglib-proxy/src/`: chat completions and embeddings take raw `Bytes` (`server.rs:418-421`, `embeddings.rs:55-58`); model load takes `Option<Json>`, `None` when no `Content-Type` is sent (`load_endpoint.rs:54-56`; axum `json.rs:123-134`); cache clear has no body and recycles an idle model (`admin.rs:36-39,92-98`).
- **[seen]** Only the proxy's `/mcp` checks `Origin` (`crates/gglib-proxy/src/mcp/handlers.rs:376-385`).

## What follows

- **[inferred]** A page open in a browser on this machine can reach every route above with a form POST or a `no-cors` fetch, and no preflight is sent: stop the daemon, switch remote access off, uninstall llama.cpp, start an MCP server, load a model, run inference. It cannot read the answer, so it cannot take an invite code.
- **[inferred]** A browser that gates a public site's requests to loopback, as Chrome's Local Network Access permission does, narrows this. A browser without such a gate does not, and whatever gets through is served. Not tried in a browser.
- **[inferred]** DELETE, PUT, PATCH and JSON-bodied routes are safe only because the browser preflights them and the allowlist refuses.

## Fix

- One origin check in `gglib-core`, derived from each router's `CorsConfig`: a request may write only if its origin may read. Same-origin passes, since `host_guard` already vouches for it; with no `Origin`, decide on `Sec-Fetch-Site`; with neither, pass, as `/mcp` does (`crates/gglib-proxy/src/mcp/handlers.rs:383`).
- Layer it on the daemon's router and the proxy's.

## Refs

#1039

title: RemoteOps::status() creates or tightens the data directory on every read
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** `RemoteOps::status` calls `identity::identity_path()` on every read (`crates/gglib-app-services/src/remote/mod.rs:227-230`), and the comment above it says so: "this touches the filesystem — creating or tightening the data directory" (`:223-226`).
- **[seen]** That is `gglib_core::paths::remote_identity_path()` (`crates/gglib-app-services/src/remote/identity.rs:36-40`), which runs `create_private_dir` on `data/` before it returns a path (`crates/gglib-core/src/paths/remote.rs:27-35`): a recursive `mkdir` at `0700`, then a `stat`, and a `chmod` when group or other holds a bit (`crates/gglib-core/src/paths/private.rs:28-31,75-81,115-122`).
- **[seen]** The same read reaches it again through `device_keys::held_ids` (`mod.rs:212`), since the daemon builds `RemoteOps` with no keys path (`crates/gglib-axum/src/config.rs:63`): `keys_path` → `device_keys_path` → `remote_identity_path()` (`crates/gglib-app-services/src/remote/device_keys.rs:155-160`, `crates/gglib-core/src/access/device_keys.rs:30-31`).
- **[seen]** The CLI's pairing screen polls status every second (`crates/gglib-cli/src/handlers/remote/pairing_tui.rs:105-112`); the desktop's serve panel polls every 15 s while a code it did not show is live (`src/components/remote/ServeSection.tsx:93-97`).

## What follows

- **[inferred]** A read path writes: two `create_private_dir` calls per status read, each a `mkdir` and at least one `stat`, on what the comment calls "the call everything else waits behind" (`mod.rs:224-225`). The cost is small; the defect is that a read does it at all, twice, on every poll.

## Fix

- Add a resolver in `gglib_core::paths` that returns the identity path without creating anything, and use it from `status` and `held_ids`.
- Keep the creating resolver for the paths that write: `arm` (`crates/gglib-app-services/src/remote/serve_arm.rs:63`) and the key store (`crates/gglib-core/src/access/device_keys.rs:80-83`).

ServeSection.tsx:93-97 polls only while pairingActive && !reveal. title: The delimited parser's deletion criterion needs a release cycle with the parser bypassed, and nothing can bypass it
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** The delimited parser's deletion criterion needs "the drift alarm … reporting zero residue across a release cycle with this parser bypassed" (`crates/gglib-core/src/normalize/parsers/delimited.rs:8-16`). `oneshot` is deleted with it (`crates/gglib-core/src/normalize/oneshot.rs:8-13`).
- **[seen]** ADR 0001 requires a Tier A behaviour to be "*skippable* when the runtime handles it natively" (`docs/adr/0001-runtime-capability-tiers.md:67-68`).
- **[seen]** `get_parser` returns the delimited parser for any resolved spec and consults no capability or switch (`crates/gglib-core/src/normalize/registry.rs:57-61`). The proxy's stream, the non-streaming path and the agent path all go through it (`crates/gglib-proxy/src/forward.rs:982`, `oneshot.rs:85`, `crates/gglib-runtime/src/ports_impl/llm_completion/stream.rs:76`).
- **[seen]** The nine `GGLIB_DISABLE_*` switches are `AGENTIC_SAMPLING`, `CACHE_AUTOSIZE`, `CACHE_REUSE`, `CONTEXT_FIT`, `GRAMMAR`, `KV_QUANT`, `MTP`, `PROMPT_CANONICALIZATION` and `TOOL_REPAIR` (`crates/gglib-core/src/debug_switches.rs:49-59`). None reaches the parser, and a test holds that list to what the tree reads (`:36-39`).
- **[seen]** The drift alarm scans text after normalization (`crates/gglib-core/src/normalize/residue.rs:6-9`), and only on the proxy's streaming path: the scanner is made, fed and read in `forward.rs` (`:990`, `:1050`, `:1227`), and neither the non-streaming path (`crates/gglib-proxy/src/unary_body.rs:149`) nor the agent path has one. The proxy's metrics store counts residue and repairs (`crates/gglib-proxy/src/metrics.rs:105,113,120`), not the calls the parser extracts.
- **[seen]** ADR 0002 found the parser never runs on the measured build, because llama-server parses the dialect first (`docs/adr/0002-defer-tool-call-constraint-to-llama-cpp.md:69-77`).

## What follows

- **[inferred]** With the parser always in the path, zero residue is what a parser that never ran and a parser that caught every leak both produce. The evidence the criterion names cannot be collected, so the parser can never meet its own deletion criterion, and `oneshot` inherits the problem.
- **[inferred]** A bypass yields evidence only where the scanner watches. Bypassed on the non-streaming or agent path, a leak would reach the client uncounted.

## Fix

- Add a `GGLIB_DISABLE_*` switch that hands the proxy's streaming path the passthrough parser while the residue scanner keeps the spec (`forward.rs:982,990`), and list it in `ALL`, so a release cycle can run with the parser off. Leave the other two paths on the parser until they have a scanner.
- Or restate the criterion around what can be measured with the parser in place, such as a new count of calls it extracted staying at zero for a release cycle. Design needed on which.

## Refs

#755, #1047

PEG_NATIVE_TOOL_CALLS is only read by launch_narration and docs, not by get_parser. Dedup: searched deletion criterion, bypass parser, residue, Tier A, GGLIB_DISABLE parser; #755 (open) item 3 asks what an inert Tier A module should do, related but not the same (it does not raise that the criterion's evidence is uncollectable); #1047 is the benchmark gap. Created rather than commented.

The scanner is made, fed and read in forward.rs:990,1050,1227; unary_body.rs:149 (non-streaming) and the agent path have none. A get_parser-wide bypass switch, as the draft's fix proposes, would let leaks through those two paths uncounted. The fix is now scoped to the streaming path. (2) The title says 'dialect parsers' (there is one) and 'cannot be exercised'; it is rewritten as a plain statement. Related to #755 item 3 but not a duplicate.

title: gglib-tauri, gglib-bootstrap and gglib-sse are thin crates, and gglib-sse's name collides with gglib_core::sse
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** Source sizes at `f07d7895` (`wc -l` over each crate's `src/*.rs`): `gglib-tauri` 76 lines in 2 files, `gglib-build-info` 167 in 1, `gglib-sse` 325 in 1 (115 of them its test module, `crates/gglib-sse/src/lib.rs:211-325`), `gglib-bootstrap` 493 in 5. Each also carries a manifest, a README and a `build.rs`.
- **[seen]** `gglib-tauri` has one dependent, `src-tauri` (`src-tauri/Cargo.toml:24`), which re-exports its `events` module (`src-tauri/src/app/events.rs:6`).
- **[seen]** `gglib-sse` is a `Broadcaster<T>` over `tokio::sync::broadcast`, served as axum `Sse` (`crates/gglib-sse/src/lib.rs:5-12`), used by `gglib-axum` and `gglib-proxy` (`crates/gglib-axum/src/sse.rs:20`, `crates/gglib-proxy/src/dashboard.rs:35`). `gglib_core::sse` is something else: the OpenAI stream decoder, encoder and frame parser (`crates/gglib-core/src/sse/mod.rs:2-8`).
- **[seen]** `gglib-bootstrap` has two dependents (`crates/gglib-axum/Cargo.toml:15`, `crates/gglib-cli/Cargo.toml:16`).
- **[seen]** `scripts/check_boundaries.sh` has rules for three of them: a dependency denylist and surface isolation for `gglib-tauri` (`:144-150`, `:157`), a denylist for `gglib-sse` (`:213-221`), and `gglib-bootstrap` as the only directory allowed to call four infrastructure entry points (`:224-243`).
- **[seen]** `gglib-build-info` has five dependents (`crates/gglib-axum/Cargo.toml:16`, `crates/gglib-cli/Cargo.toml:17`, `crates/gglib-mcp/Cargo.toml:11`, `crates/gglib-proxy/Cargo.toml:23`, `src-tauri/Cargo.toml:21`), and its 204-line `build.rs` passes through vergen's `rerun-if-changed` for `.git/HEAD` and the current ref (`crates/gglib-build-info/build.rs:93-98`).

## What follows

- **[inferred]** About 900 lines of source in `gglib-tauri`, `gglib-sse` and `gglib-bootstrap` pay for three manifests, three build scripts and three READMEs.
- **[inferred]** `gglib_sse` beside `gglib_core::sse` sends a reader to the wrong one: the name says "SSE", and only one of them parses it.
- **[inferred]** `gglib-build-info` is the one to keep apart: folded into a larger crate, its build script would rebuild that crate on every commit.

## Fix

- Fold `gglib-tauri` into `src-tauri`, its only dependent.
- Rename `gglib-sse` to say what it is (a broadcaster), or fold it and `gglib-bootstrap` into whichever crate a split of `gglib-core` puts platform code in; decide alongside that split.
- Move the `check_boundaries.sh` rules of any crate folded, in the same change; the bootstrap guard allows callers by directory.
- Leave `gglib-build-info` a leaf.

#458

## What the code does

From receipt (`crates/gglib-proxy/src/server.rs:418-421`) to the upstream send, in `crates/gglib-proxy/src/`:

- **[seen]** `canonicalize_system_prompt` parses into `Value`, and serialises when a line changed (`canonicalization.rs:157,193`; called at `server.rs:430`).
- **[seen]** `canonicalize_tool_order` parses into `Value`, and serialises when the tools are unsorted (`canonicalization.rs:226,251`; `server.rs:431`).
- **[seen]** `derive_fallback_session_id` parses into `Value` when no `x-gglib-session-id` header came (`canonicalization.rs:305`; `server.rs:469`).
- **[seen]** `extract_tool_names` parses into `Value`, at DEBUG level only (`canonicalization.rs:371,388`; `server.rs:478`).
- **[seen]** `ChatRoutingEnvelope` is a typed parse (`server.rs:486`); so is the loop guard's `scan_history` when the guard is on (`loop_guard.rs:260`, via `loop_guard_step.rs:84,100` from `server.rs:591`).
- **[seen]** A guard note parses and serialises (`loop_guard_note.rs:192,209`; `server.rs:772-775`).
- **[seen]** `shape_request_body` parses and serialises on every request (`forward.rs:442,461`; called at `forward.rs:668`). Inside it, `request_pipeline::apply` serialises the body into a byte counter to measure it (`crates/gglib-core/src/request_pipeline/truncation.rs:187,293-302`), does so again after a trim (`:241`), and for a model that needs turn coalescing converts the messages array to typed and back (`crates/gglib-core/src/request_pipeline/messages.rs:87-88,114`).
- **[seen]** `inject_streaming_body_overrides` parses and serialises on every streaming request (`forward.rs:343,359`; called at `forward.rs:797`).
- **[seen]** The `UpstreamDead` retry (`server.rs:850-982`) builds a second `ForwardRequest` field by field (`server.rs:933-964`, beside `server.rs:797-816`) and sends `body_for_retry`, so shaping and the streaming overrides run again.

## What follows

- **[inferred]** A streaming request carrying `x-gglib-session-id`, at INFO level, with the guard on and no note, is parsed from bytes six times (four into `Value`), serialised to bytes twice, and serialised once more to be measured. The most is nine parses and five serialisations to bytes, and a retry adds two of each. The code itself sizes the body at "~150KB+" (`server.rs:428-429`).
- **[inferred]** Every stage re-derives the body's shape from bytes, so a stage added later is one more full parse by default.

## Fix

- Parse into `Value` once at receipt, read the routing envelope from it, and pass `&mut Value` through canonicalisation, the guard, the note, shaping and the streaming overrides; serialise once, just before the send.
- Keep the unshaped `Value` for the `UpstreamDead` retry, which reshapes against the new context, and build both `ForwardRequest`s from one constructor.

## Refs

#644

title: gglib has no machine-readable list of the error codes its proxy writes, so clients hand-copy it
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** The proxy's JSON errors go through `ErrorResponse::with_code` (`crates/gglib-proxy/src/models.rs:422-434`). Its constructors write 14 codes: `model_loading`, `admission_timeout`, `model_not_found`, `profile_not_found`, `not_an_embedding_model`, `embedding_model_cannot_chat`, `upstream_error`, `context_length_exceeded`, `loop_detected`, `stagnation_detected`, `invalid_request`, `internal_error` (`models.rs:437-598`), `model_file_not_found` and `pinned_model_mismatch` (`:609-627`).
- **[seen]** The guards add four: `host_not_allowed` and `invalid_api_key` (`access/mod.rs:59,103`), `device_not_paired` (`remote/device_gate.rs:69`), `mcp_not_allowed_over_tunnel` (`remote/mcp_guard.rs:47`). `upstream_timeout` is written with `json!` into a stream already under way (`sse_stream.rs:147-155`). `ModelRuntimeError::Internal` goes out with no code (`models.rs:628`).
- **[seen]** No file lists them as data: the only JSON under `docs/` is two benchmark suites, and `model_loading`, `upstream_timeout` and `pinned_model_mismatch` appear in no Markdown file.
- **[seen]** ggchat hand-types all 19 (ggchat `e190a4d`, `Sources/GGChatCore/ProviderError.swift:107,117-134`). Its comment says gglib writes `invalid_pairing_code` from "its own proxy route" (`:102-106`); no gglib crate writes that code at `f07d7895`, and the proxy's router has no pairing route (`crates/gglib-proxy/src/router.rs:20-22`). ggchat #135, open, corrects that comment by hand.
- **[seen]** modelpipe publishes its codes as `docs/error-codes-v0.json`, derived from `refusal.rs` and checked by `scripts/error_codes.py --check` (modelpipe `5b86e86`, `scripts/error_codes.py:1-16`). ggchat tests against a vendored copy of that file (`Tests/GGChatCoreTests/ErrorTests.swift:43`).

## What follows

- **[inferred]** A code gglib adds, renames or retires reaches a client only when someone reads the Rust. The stale `invalid_pairing_code` note, and the hand edit now correcting it, show the copy already drifting.

## Fix

- Derive `docs/error-codes.json` (code and type) from the `ErrorResponse` constructors, the guards and the `json!` site, in the shape of modelpipe's file.
- Pin it with a test that fails when the file and the source disagree, as `error_codes.py --check` does for modelpipe.

title: The Rust file-size ratchet counts comment and blank lines
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** `scripts/check_rust_complexity.sh` sets `THRESHOLD=300` (`:27`) and sizes each `.rs` file under `crates/` and `src-tauri/` with `wc -l` (`:35-41`), so comment and blank lines count. It runs in CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:115`) and in `make` (`Makefile:268`).
- **[seen]** Measured at `f07d7895` over the 987 files it scans: 221,402 lines, of which 25.7% are `//` comment lines and 9.7% are blank. Over the 733 that are not tests (`*_tests.rs` and `tests/` left out): 161,548 lines, of which 46,876 (29.0%) are comment and 15,183 (9.4%) blank.
- **[seen]** Of the 987, 167 are over 300 by `wc -l`; 96 are over 300 counting only non-blank lines that do not start with `//`. By that count, 79 of the baseline's 175 entries are at or under 300.
- **[seen]** Files are split to satisfy it: `crates/gglib-axum/src/routes_remote.rs:3-7`, `crates/gglib-axum/src/handlers/remote/status.rs:3-6`, `crates/gglib-proxy/src/router.rs:3-5` and `crates/gglib-runtime/src/proxy/api_key.rs:3-4` each say so.

## What follows

- **[inferred]** The gate charges a line of explanation the same as a line of code, so the cheapest way under it is to delete the comments that say why, in a codebase whose conventions lean on them.
- **[inferred]** About 35% of what it measures is prose and whitespace, 38% outside tests; a 300-line non-test file here holds roughly 185 lines of code.

## Fix

- Count non-blank lines whose first non-space characters are not `//`, in both the check and `--update`.
- Rewrite the baseline once with the new count, in a commit of its own.

## Refs

#648, #1056

title: Once llama-server's headers arrive the proxy waits on it and on the client with no timer, and a non-streaming request has no bound at all
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** Once llama-server's headers arrive, the stream is drained by two `while let … .next().await` loops with no timer (`crates/gglib-proxy/src/forward.rs:959,1007`); the repair helper's docs say "the drain loop that called us has no timer" (`:1235-1236`). The only deadline is on the first byte, 300 s (`forward.rs:281`, `sse_stream.rs:97-159`), and the 15 s keepalive runs only until headers arrive (`sse_stream.rs:84-89,160-165`).
- **[seen]** Each frame goes out with `tx.send(Ok(bytes)).await` (`forward.rs:1161-1170`) on a channel 32 deep (`:828`). The send fails only once the receiving side is dropped.
- **[seen]** The upstream client has a 10 s connect timeout and, on purpose, no total timeout (`server.rs:233-255`). The non-streaming send and body read (`forward_unary.rs:64`, `unary_body.rs:73`) and the embeddings send (`embeddings.rs:186`) add none; only the repair re-issue has one (`forward_unary.rs:156`).
- **[seen]** `health_verdict` scores a turn with visible output `Healthy` even when the client left, by design (`forward.rs:184-186,194-195`).

## What follows

- **[inferred]** A client that vanishes without a FIN, such as a LAN client whose machine sleeps mid-reply, stops reading. Once 32 frames queue, `tx.send` waits until the OS gives up on the connection, and the request keeps its slot for that long. (Through the tunnel the proxy's peer is modelpipe on loopback, not the phone.)
- **[inferred]** A non-streaming or embeddings request against a wedged llama-server waits with no end.
- **[inferred]** A client that gives up on a mid-stream stall after some output is scored `Healthy`, so the watchdog never hears about the stall.
- **[inferred]** An idle bound on the upstream stream would not cover the first two, and covers the third only when it fires before the client gives up.

## Fix

Design needed. Candidates:

- A departure after N seconds of upstream silence abstains from the verdict instead of scoring `Healthy`.
- A mid-stream SSE keepalive during upstream silence, so a client is not the first to give up on a live turn.
- A bound on `tx.send`, so a reader that stopped reading releases the slot.
- A total bound on non-streaming and embeddings requests, sized like the first-byte deadline.
verification_notes: At f07d7895: forward.rs:959 byte loop and :1007 event loop, no timeout wrapper; :1235-1236 doc quote; FIRST_BYTE_DEADLINE_SECS=300 at forward.rs:281; sse_stream.rs:84-165 keepalive interval and first-byte deadline race, used only while awaiting send() (headers). tx.send at forward.rs:1161-1170, channel(32) at :828. Proxy client built at server.rs:252-255 with connect_timeout(10s) and the rationale comment :233-251. git grep for .timeout( in gglib-proxy/src: only forward.rs:1245 and forward_unary.rs:156 (repair re-issue), props.rs:222, slots.rs:321 (side calls). forward_unary.rs:64 send, unary_body.rs:73 response.bytes(), embeddings.rs:186 send - no timeout. health_verdict forward.rs:191-200 with the documented precedence at :184-186. Not verified by experiment: how long the OS takes to drop a FIN-less peer, and whether axum/hyper drops the body receiver earlier on write errors; the slot being held is inferred from the connection guard living in the stream task. The 'planned idle-timeout fix' has no issue I could find, so the body describes today's code only. Dedup: searched idle timeout, stall, mid-stream, keepalive, no timeout, FIN, client disconnect - no open match.
problems: All citations check out: the loops, the doc quote, the deadline, the channel of 32, the client builder, the unary and embeddings sends, and health_verdict. (1) The title is ungrammatical: it lists three subjects, one of which ('a client that leaves after visible output') is about scoring, not a read bound. (2) The draft uses type: fix, but gglib issues use type: bug. (3) 'A phone losing signal' is the wrong example for a FIN-less peer. Through the tunnel, the proxy's TCP peer is modelpipe on loopback, not the phone, so the example is now a LAN client with that caveat. No duplicate found.

title: gglib-core holds platform code (file and process I/O, telemetry, paths) beside the domain
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** `gglib-core` calls itself "Core domain types and port definitions" (`crates/gglib-core/Cargo.toml:5`), and turns on tokio's `fs` and `process` features (`:20`) and pulls in `tracing-subscriber` and `tracing-appender` (`:22-23`).
- **[seen]** `paths/` creates what it resolves: `data_root` makes the root when it is missing (`crates/gglib-core/src/paths/platform.rs:96-102`), and `create_private_dir`, `create_private_file` and `make_private` make and chmod `data/` and its files (`paths/private.rs:28-70`).
- **[seen]** `access/device_keys.rs` reads, writes and renames the device-key file (`:46,80-100`).
- **[seen]** `telemetry.rs` installs the global subscriber and creates the log directory (`:111-117,132`).
- **[seen]** `services/model_verification.rs` hashes model files and deletes corrupt shards (`:487-489,744`).
- **[seen]** `utils/process.rs` builds `std::process` and `tokio::process` commands (`:30-32,52-54`).
- **[seen]** The crate is 59,082 lines in 247 files under `src/`, and `request_pipeline`, `normalize`, `domain` and `ports` sit in it beside the above (`src/lib.rs:4-24`).
- **[seen]** `scripts/check_boundaries.sh` holds `gglib-core` to a dependency denylist (`axum tower tower-http clap tauri sqlx hyper`, `:111-115`) read from `cargo tree` (`:48-50`), and checks nothing about what the code does with the standard library.

## What follows

- **[inferred]** Every crate that needs the request pipeline or the domain types compiles tokio's `fs` and `process`, the log appender and the path code with them.
- **[inferred]** "Pure domain" in the boundaries script means "no adapter crates", not "no I/O", so the next module here that writes to disk passes every gate.

## Fix

- Split a domain crate (`request_pipeline`, `normalize`, `domain`, `ports`) from a platform crate (`paths`, `access`, `telemetry`, the services that touch disk).
- Make `check_boundaries.sh` fail on `std::fs`, `tokio::fs` and `tokio::process` in the domain crate.
- Settle where the thin crates go (`gglib-bootstrap`, `gglib-sse`) in the same change.

title: No gglib surface shows the device key that docs/remote.md tells a person to give a third-party client
body:
## What the code does

- **[seen]** `docs/remote.md:350-355` tells a laptop user that "Any other OpenAI-compatible client on the laptop can be pointed at the port `join` printed, `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1`, with this laptop's device key as its API key", and that the port does not add it (`:352-353`, `:568-578`).
- **[seen]** The connect panel says "A client pointed there supplies its API key" (`src/components/remote/ConnectSection.tsx:155`) and reads only whether a key is held (`:59`). The only other API-key text under `src/components/remote/` is about the serving side's proxy key (`ServeSection.tsx:152,288`).
- **[seen]** The key is `Settings.remote_pairing.api_key` (`crates/gglib-core/src/settings.rs:321`, `settings_remote.rs:56`). The desktop's settings DTO has no field for it (`crates/gglib-app-services/src/types_settings.rs:20-63`), the connect answer carries none (`crates/gglib-axum/src/handlers/remote/wire.rs:148-160`), and the status route has none by design: "device rows that have no field a key could live in" (`handlers/remote/status.rs:8-10`).
- **[seen]** `gglib config settings show` prints `remote-pairing.api-key` as "(set, not shown)" (`crates/gglib-cli/src/handlers/config/settings/settings_display.rs:29-32`).
- **[seen]** `docs/clients.md:54-56` says to use the other machine's `proxy_api_key`, and `settings_remote.rs:48-49` still describes the stored key that way; `docs/remote.md:369-376` says the edge admits only keys issued to a device: "nothing else is admitted, the desktop's own `proxy_api_key` included".

## What follows

- **[inferred]** No gglib surface hands a person the key the docs tell them to give a client, and the key `docs/clients.md` names instead is refused at the edge with a flat `401`.

## Fix

Design needed.

- A reveal-on-click for this device's key in the connect panel, behind a POST route rather than a GET, since `status.rs:8-10` keeps keys off GET. A route that returns a credential widens what a loopback caller can read, so it belongs with #1039's decision.
- The same on the CLI, where `settings show` masks the key and no `gglib remote` command prints it.
- Correct `docs/clients.md:54-56` and the doc comment at `settings_remote.rs:48-49` to name the device key.
